:::{#thm-moore-penrose-generalized-inverse}
#### A Moore-Penrose inverse is a generalized inverse

If $\matr{G}$ is a Moore-Penrose inverse of an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$ (@def-moore-penrose),
then $\matr{G}$ is a generalized inverse of $\matr{A}$ (@def-generalized-inverse).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

A generalized inverse of $\matr{A}$ is an $n \times m$ matrix $\matr{G}$ with $\matr{A}\matr{G}\matr{A} = \matr{A}$.
A Moore-Penrose inverse is an $n \times m$ matrix, and condition 1 of @def-moore-penrose is $\matr{A}\matr{G}\matr{A} = \matr{A}$.

:::

:::
